citation: Paz-Alberto, A. M., Castro, E. S., & Flores, V. L. (2006). Survey of Endemic, Indigenous and Introduced (Foreign) Species in the Freshwater Ecosystems of Nueva Ecija. Transactions of the National Academy of Science and Technology Philippines, 28(1), BSD No. 4, 52–53.

access.accessMethod: Official NAST catalog page and hosted proceedings PDF reviewed; an existing ignored local PDF copy was also hash-checked and page 52 visually inspected.

reportedMethods.fisherInterviewSample: Questionnaire distributed to 30% of the total population of fishers in each study area.

crossSourceRelationship.basis: Three authors overlap and both publications describe the same five named Nueva Ecija waters.
crossSourceRelationship.unresolved: Whether these publications report the same sampling dataset or separate/extended fieldwork is not established; do not count their totals as independent richness estimates.

limits: This proceedings item is a short abstract, not a species-by-site data table.
No field sampling dates, station coordinates, vouchers, or site-level fish labels are given in the reviewed pages.
The four native/endemic and seven introduced fish totals are study-wide aggregates; they cannot be assigned to a specific river or lake.
The source's historical labels are recorded as printed and are not silently normalized to current accepted names.
No item-specific open reuse license was identified. The review retains only short attributed summaries and does not reproduce tables or figures.
nextStep: Seek a lawful accessible copy of the 2009 full article or source-authorized underlying survey table, then reconcile field dates and per-waterbody taxa without assuming this 2006 abstract and the 2009 paper are independent surveys.
